question: Your document analysis subagent works through a long series of sources in one extended session on a single research topic. Early on, it extracted specific figures, such as a 12% adoption rate from a 2023 industry survey. Later in the session, when the coordinator asks follow-up questions, the subagent gives answers that conflict with those figures and cites "typical industry trends" instead of the specific sources. Which change most effectively addresses this problem?

options.text: Raise the max_tokens value for the subagent so that its responses have room to restate all of the earlier findings in detail.
options.reason: max_tokens limits the length of the output and does not help the subagent reliably use findings from earlier in a degraded context.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the subagent to keep its answers consistent with whatever it concluded earlier in the session.
options.reason: An instruction does not restore the specific findings that degrade in a long context; the guide's fix is to persist them in a scratchpad file the agent references.

options.text: Have the subagent record each key finding with its source in a scratchpad file and consult that file before answering later questions.
options.reason: The guide says agents should keep scratchpad files of key findings and reference them for later questions, which counteracts context degradation in extended sessions.

options.text: Have the coordinator resend the full text of every analyzed document with each follow-up question so the subagent sees all sources again.
options.reason: Resending verbose full documents fills the context even more, which worsens degradation; the guide recommends persisting compact key findings instead.
